---
name: apple-hig
description: Use when designing, implementing, or reviewing interfaces for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, visionOS, watchOS, CarPlay, or other Apple system experiences using Apple's Human Interface Guidelines. Routes to current platform, foundation, pattern, component, input, and technology guidance.
license: MIT
metadata:
  author: AyushRajSinghParihar
  source: https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines
---

# Apple Human Interface Guidelines

Use the relevant Apple guidance to make concrete design decisions. This package
contains a router, 13 family routes, 158 operational topic skills, and supporting
article-level references. It is
independent of Apple. The sources are a dated English HIG snapshot; check the
official source when a task depends on a newer release or a disputed detail.

## Route the task

1. Identify the target platform, device context, and user task from the request or
   project. Ask for the platform only when it materially affects the answer and
   cannot be inferred. Preserve the user's framework and product requirements.
2. Select the relevant family below and read that family's `SKILL.md`. Follow its
   link to the exact topic procedure under `.topics/` and read that `SKILL.md`.
   Apply its decision procedure, then consult its supporting article for facts
   and platform qualifications. Topic skills are explicitly read by installed
   file path; automatic nested discovery is not required.
   For platform support, product feasibility, or platform adaptation, first read each relevant
   platform's Getting started procedure, then the specific component or technology
   procedure. Check both the platform model and the surface's support limits.
3. Before finalizing the route, search the [complete topic index](references/topic-index.md)
   for the task's concepts as well as component or framework names. Its trigger
   descriptions connect everyday product requests to Apple's topic names; users
   need not name an Apple framework. Read the owning family and matching topic
   procedure before its supporting reference. Search relevant rows instead of
   loading the full corpus for a narrow question.
   For a screenshot-specific or animated example, also consult its
   [original visual explanation](references/media/index.md) when available.
4. Apply shared guidance and the target platform's documented differences. A
   missing platform subsection means no additional rule is stated; it does not
   prove support, nonapplicability, or identical behavior across platforms.
5. Compose families when the task crosses them: a component can also require
   accessibility, typography, localization, input, or system-experience guidance.
   Map the brief's material decisions to their owning topics. Read the owning
   procedure for each explicit concern, such as privacy or accessibility, as well
   as the affected components; a neighboring procedure's reminder is insufficient.
   Use [platform and task routes](references/platforms-and-tasks.md) when useful.
   In a review, map each supplied control to its candidate component procedure
   even when markup or behavior is missing. Use it to frame inspection questions;
   missing evidence neither proves a defect nor removes that control from scope.

All paths are relative to **this installed package**, not the shell's current
directory. No Python, network, sibling skill installation, or authoring cache is
required to read the guidance.

| Task | Read this topic skill |
|---|---|
| Platform conventions, design principles, games, device adaptation | [Getting started](subskills/apple-hig-getting-started/SKILL.md) |
| Accessibility, typography, color, materials, layout, localization, privacy | [Foundations](subskills/apple-hig-foundations/SKILL.md) |
| Onboarding, loading, search, sharing, accounts, feedback, media, settings | [Patterns](subskills/apple-hig-patterns/SKILL.md) |
| Charts, images, text views, embedded web content | [Content](subskills/apple-hig-content/SKILL.md) |
| Lists, collections, split views, tab views, disclosure and grouping | [Layout and organization](subskills/apple-hig-layout-and-organization/SKILL.md) |
| Buttons, menus, toolbars, menu bar, ornaments and actions | [Menus and actions](subskills/apple-hig-menus-and-actions/SKILL.md) |
| Sidebars, tab bars, search fields, tokens and path controls | [Navigation and search](subskills/apple-hig-navigation-and-search/SKILL.md) |
| Alerts, sheets, popovers, panels, scrolling and windows | [Presentation](subskills/apple-hig-presentation/SKILL.md) |
| Text fields, pickers, sliders, toggles, selection controls | [Selection and input](subskills/apple-hig-selection-and-input/SKILL.md) |
| Progress, activity, gauges and ratings | [Status](subskills/apple-hig-status/SKILL.md) |
| Widgets, Live Activities, notifications, Siri snippets and system surfaces | [System experiences](subskills/apple-hig-system-experiences/SKILL.md) |
| Touch, keyboard, pointer, focus, eyes, gestures, controllers and sensors | [Inputs](subskills/apple-hig-inputs/SKILL.md) |
| Apple Pay, purchases, Siri, VoiceOver, AI, CarPlay and integrations | [Technologies](subskills/apple-hig-technologies/SKILL.md) |

## Perform the requested work

Inspect the supplied brief, flow, code, specification or image before deciding
what is wrong or choosing a framework. Use the user's requested mode:

- **Design:** produce an implementable specification or interaction/state model
  from the topic's decision procedure, with concrete transitions and acceptance
  checks. Connect choices to the user's task and target platform.
- **Implement:** prefer the project's native system components when they supply
  the needed behavior. HIG explains experience requirements; verify API names,
  availability, and code against the appropriate SDK documentation. Make the
  authorized changes in the existing stack; a prose explanation alone does not
  complete an implementation request.
- **Review:** describe the observed problem, its effect, the relevant HIG rule,
  and a concrete correction. Separate source-backed findings from your own
  suggested improvements. Do not invent violations without inspecting evidence.
- **Adapt:** preserve the product task, data and useful state while applying the
  destination platform's interaction model. Patch the supplied artifact or give
  an explicit before/after contract when a design specification is requested.

Topic procedures are framework agnostic. Their worked examples and pseudocode
teach decisions, not a requirement to replace the project's technology. Load
related procedures only for a decision that actually depends on them.

Complete the topic's observable checks and report passed, failed and not executed
separately. Reading a file, citing Apple, or proposing a test does not establish
runtime behavior. Static code or screenshots cannot prove assistive-technology
order, native rendering, physical comfort, haptics, or SDK compilation.

Include official article/section links for material recommendations. Preserve
qualifications such as “consider,” “prefer,” and “avoid”; do not turn design
advice into invented universal requirements. Retain units and platform scope for
numerical specifications. If source passages conflict, describe the conflict
and the conservative application rather than silently changing the source.

## Source boundaries

This is comprehensive local guidance, not a verbatim Apple manual or an SDK API
reference. Original media explanations are supplementary to article references;
the source page remains useful for visual demonstrations. Source snapshots and
review status live in the repository's coverage report, outside ordinary skill
loading. Do not infer that a source has been independently reviewed just because
its local file exists.

Historical `navigation-bars` links now resolve to current Toolbars guidance;
`in-app-purchase` resolves to Apple In-App Purchase. The old Touch Bar and Messages
for Business HIG pages were unavailable at this snapshot. Do not fabricate their
current rules. Translations, archived pages, and complete linked SDK/WWDC libraries
are outside the source boundary.

# Apple HIG: Select the system surface before designing its content

Use this family to select and compose topic procedures. Infer the platform and
requested work from the supplied project; preserve its framework and constraints.

## Work through the decision

1. Decide whether the task needs a widget, ongoing Live Activity, notification, Siri snippet or another system-owned surface. Enter that surface’s procedure before fitting an app screen into it.
2. Specify the useful glance/action, data freshness and deep-link destination. Respect the surface’s update, interaction, presentation and privacy constraints rather than assuming full-app behavior.
3. Cover the relevant family/size, appearance, redaction, account and unavailable-data contexts. Shared surfaces require explicit decisions about whose information may be visible.
4. Deliver a surface/content/state contract and preview/check matrix; preserve documented platform support and unresolved source conflicts.

## Enter the topic procedure

Read the selected topic’s SKILL.md before its supporting guidance. For a review,
inspect actual evidence and return findings; for an implementation request, make
the authorized change; for design or adaptation, produce a usable specification
or patch. Load related topics only when the chosen procedure calls for them.

name: apple-hig-live-activities
description: Use when creating, reviewing, or adapting bounded live-event progress, compact and expanded presentations, updates, actions, and ending behavior.

# Give the live event a start and an end

Read [the Live Activities guide](../../references/live-activities.md). This workflow is application advice; destination layouts and interaction support differ.

Inspect event duration/start/end, update source, sensitivity, destinations, platform, and create/review/adapt intent. Decide whether the information is a bounded task with frequent changes or ordinary periodic widget data. Record real update/termination signals; a timer mockup is not a delivery guarantee.

Design essential iPhone compact/minimal/expanded/Lock Screen content first, retaining identity/relative positions as it expands, then tailor other destinations. Keep minimal content informative rather than a static logo. Use supported background customization only in Lock Screen, with appropriate dark/tint/Always On contrast. Favor one essential direct action and precise deep links. Protect sensitive content, omit promotion, update only changed content, and alert only for crucial updates without duplicate pushes. End immediately when the task ends and choose a useful short retained summary, not indefinite activity.

Implement the lifecycle/layouts or provide event-state/destination specifications; review exact lifecycle, privacy, or missing-presentation defects. StandBy needs scaling/red-mode checks. Watch custom layout can share CarPlay use, where controls are disabled. Mac activation uses iPhone Mirroring; tvOS/visionOS are unsupported. Do not reuse a control-dependent watch layout as a driving workflow.

**Worked transformation:** Before: a courier activity runs after delivery, exposes a full address, and requires Pause on CarPlay. Decision: the task is over, private information is excessive, and driving controls are disabled. After: end at delivery, retain a brief safe summary where allowed, show only necessary destination context, and make CarPlay status useful without interaction.

Deliver the artifact, state lifecycle, update/alert policy, all relevant presentations, and destinations. Verify multiple activities/minimal state, completion, stale updates, red/Always On, and control-disabled destinations. Fail for unbounded lifecycle, misleading status, duplicate alerts, or unsupported interaction. Actual push delivery/native rendering/device behavior requires execution evidence.

Load [widgets](../apple-hig-widgets/SKILL.md) for periodic data, [notifications](../apple-hig-notifications/SKILL.md) for separate events, or [app-shortcuts](../apple-hig-app-shortcuts/SKILL.md) for relevant initiation.

name: apple-hig-privacy
description: Use when designing or reviewing permission timing, purpose strings, pre-permission explanations, tracking requests, data minimization, or private platform inputs.

# Ask for precise access when its purpose is clear

Read [Privacy](../../references/privacy.md). Inspect the feature's actual data needs, transfers, storage, current permission flow, and supported platform. Establish design, review, or adaptation mode. Produce the requested copy/flow/data-handling changes in the existing stack; distinguish documented platform restrictions from additional application recommendations.

Map each requested category to a specific feature and minimum necessary scope. Remove collection without a concrete benefit; prefer on-device work where it avoids unnecessary transfer. Explain collection/use accurately and flag App Store disclosure updates needed when behavior changes. Respect private email and tracking choices rather than designing around them.

Ask when the person invokes the feature. Launch-time requests need an essential, obvious dependency. Write a short active purpose sentence explaining use and reason. If context is sufficient, omit a custom pre-alert; if explanation is essential, use one clear continuation to the real system alert without imitating Allow/Don't Allow. Keep the guide's special pre-alert restrictions distinct from ordinary onboarding. Tracking requires its system authorization before collection and must not be incentivized or manipulated.

Choose one-time location access for suitable individual tasks using the system location button on supported platforms; preserve permitted customization and all localized/accessibility-sized text. Protect secrets with established authentication/keychain mechanisms. For Mac, account for sandboxing/distribution and fast user switching. For visionOS, separate system rendering assistance from permission-gated Full Space ARKit data; gaze remains private, and imported phone-camera assumptions may need removal or content import.

**Before → decision → after:** A bird journal asks for contacts, microphone, and continuous location at launch although only “Attach current location” uses location. Decision: request only the specific action's needed access. After, journaling works immediately; the attachment action offers the supported location control, and its purpose explains adding the sighting's location.

Deliver a data-purpose/access matrix and corrected permission sequence/copy or implementation. Fail if collection precedes required consent, copy obscures the real use, or unrelated work is gated on optional access. Report code/flow evidence separately from actual authorization prompts and privacy-setting behavior; this procedure does not certify security or legal compliance.

Use [Sign in with Apple](../../../apple-hig-technologies/.topics/apple-hig-sign-in-with-apple/SKILL.md) for that authentication choice and [Augmented reality](../../../apple-hig-technologies/.topics/apple-hig-augmented-reality/SKILL.md) when room/camera access is essential.

# Live Activities Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/live-activities) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. ## Contents - [Anatomy](#Anatomy) - [Best practices](#Best-practices) - [Presentation](#Presentation) - [CarPlay](#CarPlay) - [Platform considerations](#Platform-considerations) - [Specifications](#Specifications) Live Activities track a bounded task or event through frequent updates over a few hours. They begin on iPhone or iPad and can appear on the Lock/Home Screen, Dynamic Island and StandBy, paired Mac menu bar, Apple Watch Smart Stack, and CarPlay Dashboard. ## Anatomy Support compact, minimal, expanded, and Lock Screen presentations. The system composes these for available space and devices. ### Compact A single Dynamic Island activity uses separate leading/trailing elements around the TrueDepth camera. ### Minimal Multiple activities use compact circular/oval treatments, up to three where supported: one attached and others detached. Tap opens the app; hold expands. ### Expanded Holding compact/minimal content reveals a larger presentation. ### Lock Screen A bottom banner uses a layout related to expanded. On devices without Dynamic Island, essential update alerts can briefly overlay this banner on Home or another app. ### StandBy Minimal content expands on tap to a Lock Screen layout scaled 2×. A custom background extends across the screen. ## Best practices Use tasks with clear starts and ends, ideally no more than 8 hours. Show only immediately useful information, with details in the app. Exclude ads and promotions. Avoid exposed sensitive content; summarize or redact and offer app access/configuration. Match app identity across appearances; a logo mark can appear without a container, but do not use the full app icon. Do not draw attention to Dynamic Island from inside the app. Use legible large text, generally medium weight or stronger. ### Creating Live Activity layouts Adapt to actual screens and scale factors. Keep layout only as large as content needs. For limited-width Dynamic Island contexts, fit compact/minimal content within a 28-pt circle with abbreviations or graphics; use leading-only when a meaningful trailing version cannot fit. Favor familiar templates, even concentric margins, and container-relative corner radii. Inset groups or use a thick dividing line instead of extending content to edges. A blurred drawing-tool preview can help align angular content within rounded corners. Adjust Lock Screen/expanded height as available information grows or shrinks. ### Choosing colors Only Lock Screen permits custom background colors; compact, minimal, and expanded backgrounds are system-controlled. Dynamic Island is opaque black, so meaningful bold foreground color can express identity. Match its dark-background keyline to related content. Check custom Lock Screen contrast in both appearances and reduced-luminance Always On. ### Adding transitions and animating content updates Animations can last at most 2 seconds and are not played in reduced-luminance Always On. Use numeric changes, fades, scale, or movement to explain updates. Preserve existing elements as layout grows rather than removing/readding everything. Avoid transition collisions; animate a moved item and fade other list elements when needed. ### Offering interactivity Deep-link to the relevant task. Favor one essential button or toggle for a direct action, pause/resume, or response to meaningful progress, preserving space for status and reducing accidental activation. ### Starting, updating, and ending a Live Activity Begin at expected moments, including automatic starts for followed events, with an easy opt-out in the corresponding app view. Offer an App Shortcut when useful. Update only for changed content. Alert only for crucial updates and avoid a parallel push for the same information. Prefer one dynamically changing activity for related simultaneous events. End immediately when the task ends: Dynamic Island/CarPlay remove it, while Lock Screen, Mac, and watch can retain it for up to 4 hours. Choose a shorter useful summary lifetime, commonly 15–30 minutes, proportional to the activity. ## Presentation Design the iPhone presentations first, then tailor layouts for StandBy, watch, and driving while supporting every destination. ### Compact presentation Show essential changing data. Make both halves read as one through coherent color/type and balanced widths. Fit snugly against the camera without extra inner padding or unnecessary status-bar obstruction; shorten units or precision as needed. Both halves should deep-link to the same relevant app screen. ### Minimal presentation Preserve recognition while conveying current information instead of only a static logo. ### Expanded presentation Expand predictably from the smaller layout, retaining relative positions and fitting content close to the camera rather than leaving unused gaps. ### Lock Screen presentation Create a distinct task layout rather than copying notification structure. Use restrained tint/background customization to fit personalized wallpapers. Verify contrast in both appearances and Always On, including the system-generated dismiss-button color; override its foreground if needed. Standard margins are 14 pt, with tighter spacing only when content grouping needs it. ### StandBy presentation Supply assets and, where useful, a custom layout for the larger scale. The default background blends with the bezel and surroundings and permits slightly more content scale. Preserve margins so expansion does not crop graphics, and test the red-tinted Night Mode. ## CarPlay The default combines compact halves. A supplemental small family can support larger type and more information. Its custom layout is also used on watch, but CarPlay disables buttons and toggles; driving-oriented activities should prioritize timely content over those controls. ## Platform considerations No additional iOS or iPadOS rules are specified. Live Activities are unsupported in tvOS and visionOS. ### macOS Paired Mac menu-bar presentations use compact/minimal/expanded styles. Activation opens the app through iPhone Mirroring. ### watchOS The activity appears atop the paired watch's Smart Stack, combining compact halves by default. Tap opens a watch app when available; otherwise it opens a full-screen view with a paired-iPhone launch button. A custom layout can improve essential progress, changes, and controls, but consider its shared use in CarPlay where interaction is disabled. ## Specifications These source dimensions are design guidance in points; Communicate collection and usage clearly and protect granted data. Request at launch only when access is essential and obviously necessary, such as location for navigation or room information for a spatial game that needs walls. item.text: The proposal contains five verified problems: promotional use without an active delivery, an exposed address, a stale estimate labeled “Now,” indefinite completion display, and a catalog in expanded content. I’ll specify an event-driven lifecycle and privacy-safe content, keeping proposed timing policies distinct from HIG guidance.

# Delivery Live Activity review

Reviewed "'`interface.md` as an iOS iPhone Lock Screen proposal. Decision: revise before implementation. All five findings below are verified against the supplied text; severity ranks are review judgments, not Apple classifications. No rendered interface or executable implementation was supplied.

## Ranked findings and decisions

| Rank | Observed evidence | Effect and source-backed decision | Corrected behavior |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 — High | “shows the customer’s full address on Lock Screen” | Exposes personal destination information on a glanceable surface. Live Activities guidance says to avoid exposed sensitive content and summarize or redact. | Omit the address from the activity payload and every presentation. Show “Your delivery”; open the relevant order in the app for destination details, subject to the app’s authentication policy. |
| 2 — High | “starts automatically for promotional offers with no active delivery” | Has no bounded live task and uses the surface for promotion. Automatic initiation itself is not the defect: expected automatic starts for followed events are permitted. | Create an activity only for a real, active delivery the person expects to track, with an easy opt-out in that order’s app view. Keep offers in the app. |
| 3 — High | “labels a 40-minute-old estimate Now” | Misrepresents old information as current and undermines the central tracking task. The topic procedure explicitly fails misleading status; the guide requires immediately useful changing information. | Track estimate observation time and validity separately from arrival time. For this stale sample show “Arrival estimate unavailable · Last update 40 min ago.” Never infer arrival or delivery from elapsed time. |
| 4 — Medium | “keeps displaying Delivered forever” | Leaves an unbounded activity after the task ends. Guidance says end immediately; retained Lock Screen summaries are distinct from active tracking. | End on a confirmed terminal event. Request a short retained “Delivered” summary for 15 minutes, then removal. System/user removal may happen earlier; indefinite retention is disallowed. |
| 5 — Medium | “puts a complete shopping catalog inside expanded content” | Crowds out delivery progress and turns a glanceable task surface into an app screen. Guidance says show immediately useful information and keep details in the app. | Expanded content contains delivery identity, confirmed phase, trustworthy estimate or freshness fallback, and a relevant order deep link. Shopping stays in the app. |

Sources for ranks 1, 2, and 5: [Live Activities — Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/live-activities#Best-practices). Rank 3 also applies the installed Live Activities topic procedure’s misleading-status check and [Presentation](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/live-activities#Presentation). Rank 4 and initiation/update decisions: [Starting, updating, and ending a Live Activity](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/live-activities#Starting-updating-and-ending-a-Live-Activity). Data minimization is also supported by [Privacy — Best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/privacy#Best-practices).

## Framework-agnostic corrected contract

The following timing and copy choices are product decisions: a 5-minute estimate freshness budget and a 15-minute retained terminal summary. They are not mandatory HIG constants. Validate the freshness budget with the delivery data provider. The local guide recommends a shorter useful retained summary, commonly 15–30 minutes, within the system’s stated maximum of 4 hours; it describes bounded tasks ideally no longer than 8 hours, not an invented universal runtime guarantee.

```text
Inputs:
  deliveryId, accountId, expectedTracking, trackingAllowed
  event { revision, observedAt, phase, estimateWindow?, estimateValidUntil? }
  phase = preparing | enRoute | delivered | cancelled

Public presentation model:
  safeDeliveryLabel, confirmedPhase, estimateWindow?, observedAt,
  estimateValidUntil?, orderDestination
  // No street address, unit, access code, customer name, or catalog.

Start:
  if real delivery is active AND expectedTracking AND trackingAllowed:
    create one activity associated with this delivery
  otherwise: do not create
  promotions never create or update an activity

Receive event:
  verify association with delivery/account
  reject older or duplicate revisions
  accept confirmed phase from authoritative delivery events
  if delivered OR cancelled:
    publish safe terminal summary
    end active tracking immediately
    request retained summary expiry = terminal receipt time + 15 minutes
    reject later nonterminal events for this completed delivery
  else:
    update only changed content

Render estimate at current time:
  fresh = estimate exists
          AND 0 <= now - observedAt <= 5 minutes
          AND (estimateValidUntil absent OR now < estimateValidUntil)
  if fresh: show absolute arrival window and update age
  else: show "Arrival estimate unavailable" and last-update age
  missing or invalid timestamp: show "Update time unavailable"
  never show "Now" solely because an estimate time has passed

Navigation and exit:
  activity activation -> app'"'s matching order details
  order view -> easy tracking opt-out
  opt-out -> end activity without a retained summary
  account change -> remove previous account's activity
  dismissal does not cancel the delivery or automatically recreate tracking
"'```

The data source must emit real phase changes, including terminal events. A timer cannot establish delivery. Estimate expiry needs a platform-supported stale-state mechanism or scheduled update strategy; unavailable delivery must produce conservative fallback content. This document does not establish that background updates or removal will execute reliably. On reconnect, reconcile the authoritative order state before presenting a fresh estimate. Terminal states cannot be reversed by a late en-route update.

Alert only for crucial changes, for example confirmed arrival when useful to receive the order. Do not also send a push for the same information. No alerts for unchanged data or estimate aging. This example is a product policy under [Live Activities lifecycle guidance](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/live-activities#Starting-updating-and-ending-a-Live-Activity).

### Presentation and data decisions

| Surface/context | Required content and behavior |
|---|---|
| Lock Screen | “Your delivery,” confirmed phase, fresh arrival window or explicit stale fallback. Terminal summary replaces tracking after completion. Use only necessary height, standard 14 pt margins unless grouping justifies tighter spacing, and legible text generally medium weight or stronger. |
| Expanded | Preserve identity and relative status positions from compact; add freshness detail. No catalog. |
| Compact | Coherent leading delivery identity/phase and trailing fresh estimate or stale indicator; both halves open the same order. |
| Minimal / multiple activities | Recognizable delivery symbol plus changing phase or stale indicator; not a static logo alone. Distinguish simultaneous orders with safe labels when necessary. |
| Always On / appearances | Same privacy-safe content; verify foreground, background, and dismiss-control contrast in light, dark, and reduced luminance. Do not depend on animation to communicate status. |
| StandBy / propagated destinations | Verify scaled layout, margins and red Night Mode. Preserve essential status without controls for CarPlay; paired watch/Mac behavior needs separate execution checks if supported by the implementation. |

These are specifications, not verified layouts. See [Presentation](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/live-activities#Presentation), [Lock Screen presentation](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/live-activities#Lock-Screen-presentation), and [CarPlay](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/live-activities#CarPlay). The local guide’s sample iPhone Lock Screen sizes are 408×84–160 pt for a 430×932 pt screen and 371×84–160 pt for a 393×852 pt screen; these are contextual design guidance, not universal fixed dimensions.

No buttons, toggles, or other explicit controls are supplied in `interface.md`, so no existing control semantics or target sizes can be audited. The proposed activation destination is a deep link, not a new direct-action button. If a direct action is later added, review its owning component procedure; the guide favors one essential button or toggle rather than filling expanded content with controls: [Offering interactivity](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/live-activities#Offering-interactivity).

| Data | Purpose / exposure decision |
|---|---|
| Full destination address | Needed for fulfillment and order details; excluded from public activity content. No conclusion about existing collection, storage, or permissions is possible. |
| Phase, estimate, observation time | Minimum tracking information; display with explicit freshness semantics. |
| Internal order/account identifiers | Associate events and route to the correct order; do not render publicly. |
| Catalog and offers | No delivery-progress purpose; excluded from activity. |

No new location or other permission request is specified. Whether any permission flow needs revision is unknown because none was supplied.

## Worked before/after

Illustrative clock times below make the supplied 40-minute age concrete; they are not additional observations.

| Moment | Before from proposal | After under this contract |
|---|---|---|
| Offer received; no delivery | Promotional activity starts automatically. | No activity is created. Offer remains in app. |
| 13:55, actual order active | Full address appears publicly; expanded catalog is available. | “Your delivery · On the way · Estimated 14:20–14:30 · Updated just now.” Activation opens this order. |
| 14:35, no update since 13:55 | Estimate is labeled “Now.” | “Your delivery · On the way · Arrival estimate unavailable · Last update 40 min ago.” Phase is the last confirmed phase, not proof of current courier position. |
| 14:42, authoritative delivered event | “Delivered” remains forever. | End active tracking immediately; request safe “Delivered at 14:42” Lock Screen summary until 14:57. Dynamic Island removes the ended activity. |
| 14:57 | Still “Delivered.” | No retained activity requested; historical details remain in the order view. |

## Acceptance checks and current status

**Passed — static review only:** inspected all supplied interface text; tied each of its five claims to a ranked correction; read installed root → system-experiences family → Live Activities topic → guide, plus foundations → Privacy topic → guide; searched the topic index before finalizing routing. Corrected contract specifies start, freshness, terminal events, removal, destinations, privacy, and relevant presentations.

**Failed — supplied proposal by textual inspection:** all five ranked requirements: appropriate nonpromotional start, safe public content, truthful freshness, bounded completion, and task-focused expanded content. “Verified” means explicitly stated in the proposal, not observed on a device.

**Not executed — implementation acceptance:**

- No delivery + offer event creates zero activities; expected active delivery creates one; opt-out prevents recreation.
- Serialization and every presentation contain no full address or other excluded sensitive values, including when locked or Always On.
- A 40-minute-old estimate uses stale fallback; test missing timestamps, clock skew, expiration, reconnection, and late/duplicate revisions. Aging must invalidate the display without a new server event.
- A delivered/cancelled event ends active tracking immediately; retained summary expires under the chosen policy; late nonterminal events cannot revive it. Test user dismissal and account switching.
- Expanded content has only delivery essentials; compact halves open the same order; minimal remains informative with competing activities.
- Only changed content updates; crucial alerts have no duplicate push. Verify real event delivery and termination during app inactivity/network loss.
- Preview representative iPhone sizes, long localized labels, enlarged text, light/dark wallpaper, Always On and dismiss-control contrast; check reading order and meaningful spoken status with assistive technology. Check StandBy red mode and any propagated destinations. These are unresolved checks, not verified defects.

## Evidence limits

Only `interface.md` and installed local guidance were used; no web browsing occurred. Official links identify the source guidance and were not fetched. The local Live Activities guide records a 2026-10-25 snapshot; Privacy records retrieval on that date. Installed guidance is an independently authored HIG snapshot, not an SDK reference or proof of current API availability. No source conflict relevant to these decisions was found in the read passages.

There is no screenshot, layout, payload, backend event stream, SDK, build, GUI, device, or accessibility execution evidence. Therefore this audit cannot establish contrast, clipping, actual background delivery, dismissal timing, API feasibility, or assistive-technology behavior. The corrected artifact is a reviewable specification; it is not a tested implementation or security/privacy certification.
EOF'

For this stale sample show “Arrival estimate unavailable · Last update 40 min ago.” Never infer arrival or delivery from elapsed time. |
| 4 — Medium | “keeps displaying Delivered forever” | Leaves an unbounded activity after the task ends. Guidance says end immediately; retained Lock Screen summaries are distinct from active tracking. | End on a confirmed terminal event. Request a short retained “Delivered” summary for 15 minutes, then removal. System/user removal may happen earlier; indefinite retention is disallowed. |
